title: Skill card
goal: Read one skill's card for one discipline: how to interpret answers, then what to ask.
primaryQuestion: How do I interview for this skill in this discipline?
_why: One long page read top to bottom, in the order of the card's two jobs: interpret first (descriptors, then topics as the bridge, then signals), ask second (questions, practical tasks), flags last. No tabs on purpose — an interviewer reads in sequence during preparation and mid-interview. The template's aside carries a plain-anchor 'on this page' list. The header carries the skill name ONLY (no text under titles, system rule); the global description, the card's group and which disciplines have cards live in the About section as content, shown with or without a card — the skill is global, only the card is per discipline. The discipline SegmentedControl repeats in the page actions because HERE it decides which card is open: same control, and on this screen its consequence is visible — switching to a discipline without a card lands on the explicit no-card state.

zones.name: header
zones.purpose: The discipline switch (SegmentedControl) in the page actions. Every discipline is offered even when it has no card for this skill: choosing it shows the no-card state, which is information, not a dead end.

zones.name: about
zones.purpose: The global half of the skill, as content rather than header text: the description, which disciplines have cards, and — when a card is open — its group. Rendered with or without a card, because the skill exists either way.

zones.name: descriptors
zones.answers: How do I interview for this skill in this discipline?
zones.purpose: Proficiency descriptors, the interpret job: a flat four-row Table, Novice to Expert, each row a short placeholder descriptor naming its field ('Descriptor for Novice: 2-3 sentences…'). Flat because it is read as a scale, not as four cards.

zones.name: topics
zones.purpose: The card's topics as a flat cloud of Tags — name only, exactly what the model stores in the first pass. No importance, no nesting, no expand.

zones.name: signals
zones.purpose: Behavioural signals in three blocks — strong, moderate, weak — each headed by a Badge carrying its proficiency range, over a plain list of placeholder signs.

zones.name: questions
zones.purpose: Questions, the ask job: filtered to one proficiency at a time by a SegmentedControl (All | Novice | Intermediate | Advanced | Expert), the items grouped under a proficiency subhead — no badge per row, a line-start label breaks the reading flow and the group says it once. Placeholder: two questions per proficiency, each naming its field.

zones.name: tasks
zones.purpose: Practical tasks, mirroring the questions block exactly: the same proficiency filter, the same grouped shape.

zones.name: flags
zones.purpose: Red flags and yellow flags as two plain lists under their subheads — the subhead names the colour once, the rows stay readable. The interpret job's last word.

states.empty: EmptyState surface=page icon=info when this skill has no card in the chosen discipline: names the disciplines that do have one, and the action switches to the first of them. The global skill header stays — the skill exists, only the card is absent.
states.error: EmptyState surface=page icon=folder when the skill id in the URL matches nothing: offers the way back to the skill catalog.

data: card for (skill, current discipline): descriptors per proficiency, topics, signals with ranges, questions and tasks tagged by proficiency, red and yellow flags

behaviours.given: a skill that has a card in .NET and none in Java
behaviours.when: the reader switches the card screen to Java
behaviours.then: the card lookup returns nothing, the screen shows the explicit no-card state naming which disciplines have one, and the skill's own header stays in place
behaviours.why: The split the target model introduces: the skill is global, the card is per discipline. Hiding the skill or erroring would re-merge the two, which is the old model's defect.
